You are doing functional research for "Atlas ERP", an open-source ERP whose explicit benchmark is SAP S/4HANA. Your assigned S/4HANA area: Production Planning (PP).

TASK: Establish what this area actually covers in current S/4HANA (2025/2026), identify the 6-12 capabilities practitioners consider essential, and judge each against the planned Atlas v1 scope below.

METHOD: Use WebSearch (and WebFetch for promising pages) - 2 to 5 targeted searches. Prefer SAP Help Portal, SAP Community, and reputable ERP consulting sources. If web tools are unavailable or consistently fail, fall back to your embedded knowledge of S/4HANA and say so explicitly in the overview field.

COVER AT MINIMUM: Bills of material, work centers, routings, production orders, MRP and MRP Live, capacity planning, plus what v1-grade systems typically omit (kanban, repetitive manufacturing, detailed scheduling/PPDS).

PLANNED ATLAS V1 SCOPE FOR THIS AREA (judge full/partial/out-of-scope against THIS, not your own ideas):
Multi-level versioned BOMs; work centers; routings with setup/run times; production orders (reserve materials, issue to WIP, finish to stock, WIP journals); MRP run exploding sales-order demand + reorder points against supply producing planned orders; rough capacity check (work-center load vs available hours).

RULES:
- atlas_v1 = "full" when Atlas v1 plans the practitioner-essential core of the capability; "partial" when a meaningful but reduced subset is planned; "out-of-scope" when none of it is planned.
- Every "partial" and "out-of-scope" entry MUST have a non-empty reason (why cut / where the boundary sits) and later_path (how to add it later in one line).
- atlas_module must be one of: finance, inventory, procurement, sales, manufacturing, quality, maintenance, hr, projects, crm, reporting, admin, industry, core, frontend, or "-" for out-of-scope.
- Be honest: if S/4HANA has an essential capability the Atlas plan misses entirely, include it as out-of-scope rather than omitting it.

Your final output is consumed by a script - return only the structured data.

Based on the search results, here's an overview of the key capabilities of the SAP S/4HANA Production Planning (PP) module:

## Core Production Planning Capabilities

SAP PP is a module used for planning and managing manufacturing processes like production orders, material requirements, and capacity planning.

### Key Functional Areas

**1. Material Requirements Planning (MRP)**
MRP Live is one of the most significant updates in SAP S/4HANA, executing planning calculations in-memory and delivering results in minutes, even for large datasets. MRP Live offers far more options for selecting relevant parameters, such as multiple plants, materials, and MRP controllers.

**2. Production Order Management**
The PP module enables the creation and management of production orders to execute the manufacturing process, including functionalities for order release, capacity planning, and shop floor control.

**3. Capacity Planning**
Capacity Planning is used to analyze the capacity overloads at work center and shift the orders to avoid any capacity bottlenecks. Capacity leveling lets planners shift workloads, sometimes automatically, sometimes manually, until the schedule becomes feasible again.

**4. Demand Management and Forecasting**
The PP module supports demand forecasting and the creation of production plans based on customer demands, sales forecasts, and inventory levels.

**5. Master Data Management**
SAP S/4HANA PP allows organizations to manage master data related to production, including material master data, bills of materials (BOMs), work centers, and routing information.

### Advanced Features

S/4HANA introduces predictive planning capabilities in SAP PP, leveraging AI and machine learning for improved planning accuracy, with Predictive MRP using historical data to forecast future material requirements.

While the basic production planning functions are available in the SAP S/4HANA Digital Core ERP-PP (MRP, CRP) embedded PP/DS provides additional advanced options for Production Planning and Detailed Scheduling.

Based on my web search for SAP S/4HANA production planning and related topics, here's what I found:

## Demand Management and Planned Independent Requirements

Demand management is the management of independent requirements. Planned independent requirements are stock requirements and can be derived from a forecast of future demands. Planned independent requirements (PIR) are stock requirements and might initiate procurement or production without waiting for sales orders, and these requirements for a certain material in a certain plant are derived from a forecast of the future requirements situation or can be created manually.

## Production Versions and Order Management

Production versions are used to link materials, work centers, and routings. The PP module enables the creation and management of production orders to execute the manufacturing process, and includes functionalities for order release, capacity planning, and shop floor control.

## Shop Floor Control

Shop floor control involves examining how discrete manufacturing processes are executed in SAP S/4HANA, focusing on production orders and detailed scheduling.

## Integration and Planning Tools

PP/DS (Production Planning/Detailed Scheduling) is the standard solution for production planning in S/4HANA, serving as an ideal complement to Integrated Business Planning in the cloud. PIRs represent forecasted demand independent of customer orders.

The search results provide comprehensive information on these SAP S/4HANA production planning components and their interrelationships in the manufacturing process.

# SAP PP in S/4HANA: Main Components & Capabilities

Based on the guide, here are the core components:

## Master Data
- **Material Master**: Controls planning type, lot sizing, and availability checks for every material
- **Bill of Materials (BOM)**: "Defines what goes into the product i.e. components, quantities, sometimes even scrap percentages"
- **Routing**: Step-by-step manufacturing process linked to operations and work centers
- **Work Centers**: Physical or logical production resources with scheduling rules and costing

## Planning & Execution
- **Demand Management**: Creates Planned Independent Requirements (PIRs) as forecasts to drive MRP
- **MRP (Material Requirements Planning)**: "The engine that calculates what needs to be produced, in what quantity, and when"
- **Production Orders**: "Where planning starts to become real" with order type selection and scheduling
- **Confirmations**: Time and quantity recording that updates the system

## Optimization
- **Capacity Planning & Leveling**: "Calculates needs per operation" and adjusts workloads to avoid overloads
- **PP/DS (Production Planning/Detailed Scheduling)**: Advanced algorithms handling complex manufacturing scenarios
- **Quality Management Integration**: Builds quality checks directly into the manufacturing process

Each component interconnects through master data to align production with demand and supply constraints.

input.overview: Findings are based on live web research (SAP Help Portal, SAP Learning, SAP Community/SAP PRESS blogs, and practitioner guides) for current S/4HANA 2025/2026. S/4HANA PP covers manufacturing master data (material master, multi-level BOMs, work centers, routings, production versions), demand management with planning strategies and planned independent requirements, MRP including the in-memory MRP Live engine, production order execution with shop floor control and confirmations, and capacity evaluation/leveling. It additionally ships lean/order-less execution models (kanban, repetitive manufacturing), process-industry variants (PP-PI), and embedded PP/DS for finite detailed scheduling and optimization. Atlas v1's plan covers the discrete-manufacturing core well (BOMs, work centers, routings, production orders with WIP accounting, a deterministic MRP run, rough capacity check) while deliberately omitting forecast-based demand management, operation-level confirmations, capacity leveling, kanban, repetitive manufacturing, PP-PI, and PP/DS-class finite scheduling — the same areas v1-grade systems typically defer.

capabilities.description: Defines product structure per level with components, quantities, scrap, validity dates/change numbers, and alternatives; basis for MRP explosion and order reservations.
capabilities.later_path: Alternative BOMs, engineering change management, and variant configuration can be layered on the versioned BOM model later.

capabilities.description: Master data for machines/lines/labor pools holding capacity (available hours), scheduling formulas, and costing links used by routings and capacity planning.
capabilities.later_path: Shift calendars, capacity categories, and cost-center activity rates can be added incrementally.

capabilities.description: Step-by-step operations assigned to work centers with standard values (setup, machine/run, labor) driving scheduling and product costing; combined with BOMs via production versions.
capabilities.later_path: Sub-operations, parallel/alternative sequences, and external-processing (subcontract) operations can be added to the routing model later.

capabilities.description: Create/release orders from planned orders, reserve components, goods issue to WIP, goods receipt to stock, status management, and WIP/settlement postings to accounting.
capabilities.later_path: Rework orders, co-products, availability checks at release, and order splitting can be added on the same order object.

capabilities.description: Recording yield, scrap, and actual setup/machine/labor times per routing operation, triggering backflush, WIP valuation, and progress tracking.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans only order-level completion (issue to WIP, finish to stock, WIP journals); per-operation confirmations with actual time capture and scrap recording are not planned.
capabilities.later_path: Add a confirmation entity keyed to routing operations that posts actual times/quantities into the existing WIP journals.

capabilities.description: Net-requirements calculation exploding demand through BOM levels against stock and supply, generating planned orders/purchase requisitions; MRP Live runs it in-memory across plants in minutes with exception messages and rescheduling proposals.
capabilities.reason: The core deterministic run (sales-order demand + reorder points exploded against supply, producing planned orders) is planned; exception/rescheduling messages, MRP areas, multi-plant scope, net-change planning, and MRP-Live-class in-memory performance are not.
capabilities.later_path: Layer exception messages, pegging, and net-change/multi-plant runs onto the same planning engine without schema changes.

capabilities.description: Compares work-center load from planned/production orders against available capacity, then levels by dispatching/shifting operations to resolve overloads.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans capacity evaluation only (rough load vs available hours per work center); interactive leveling, dispatching, and finite scheduling are not planned.
capabilities.later_path: Add a dispatching board that re-dates order operations against a finite work-center calendar using the existing load data.

capabilities.capability: Demand management and planning strategies (PIRs, MTS/MTO)
capabilities.description: Maintains planned independent requirements from forecasts, applies planning strategies (make-to-stock, make-to-order, assembly), and consumes forecast against incoming sales orders.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 MRP consumes only direct sales-order demand and reorder points; forecast-based PIRs, planning strategies, and forecast-consumption logic are not planned, so make-to-stock forecast planning is impossible in v1.
capabilities.later_path: Add a PIR table with strategy/consumption rules as an additional demand source feeding the existing MRP run.

capabilities.description: Control cycles with container statuses (full/empty) that trigger replenishment via in-house production, external procurement, or stock transfer without MRP planning per bin.
capabilities.reason: No pull/lean replenishment is planned; Atlas v1 is purely push-based (MRP plus reorder points), which is the typical v1-grade boundary.
capabilities.later_path: Add kanban control cycles whose status changes generate the existing supply elements (production orders/purchase orders/transfers).

capabilities.description: Order-less, rate-based production on lines using run schedules and backflush confirmations against production versions, with period-based cost collectors instead of discrete orders.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 supports only discrete production orders; period/rate-based order-less execution and product cost collectors are not planned.
capabilities.later_path: Add run-schedule headers on production versions with backflush postings reusing BOM/routing and inventory movement logic.

capabilities.description: Advanced finite-capacity scheduling embedded in S/4HANA: sequencing, setup-matrix optimization, pegging, heuristics, and a graphical planning board for bottleneck resources.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 stops at rough infinite-capacity load checks; finite scheduling, optimizers, and planning boards are deliberately omitted, as in virtually all v1-grade ERPs.
capabilities.later_path: Bolt on a finite-scheduler service consuming routings, work-center calendars, and order operations via the existing APIs.

capabilities.capability: Process manufacturing (PP-PI: master recipes, process orders)
capabilities.description: Industry variant for batch/process industries using master recipes, resources, process orders, process instructions/PI sheets, and batch management integration.
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 targets discrete manufacturing only; recipe/process-order semantics, PI sheets, and phase-based execution are not planned.
capabilities.later_path: Model recipes and process orders as specializations of routings/production orders in a later industry add-on.
